2 years hands on experience in a vehicle maintenance shop environment performing a variety of duties repairing light and heavy-duty vehicles.

Vehicle Inspection, Diagnosis, Repair, and Maintenance • Inspects University vehicles and equipment to determine necessary maintenance and repairs. • Performs automotive maintenance and repairs, including major mechanical repairs, engine work, tune-ups, brake service, transmission and differential repairs, and related automotive systems work. • Responds to equipment malfunctions, mechanical issues, and vehicle repair needs in support of Fleet Services operations. • Operates tow trucks and related equipment to move University vehicles and equipment, including field support for disabled vehicles and equipment movement. • Assists other technicians as needed to support timely completion of work. (55% time)

Shop Operations, Equipment, Records, and Inventory • Keeps the shop, tools, equipment, service yard, and gas/fuel island clean, organized, secured, and in safe operating condition in compliance with applicable OSHA requirements, University safety procedures, and department standards. • Operates, cleans, maintains, and accounts for automotive shop equipment, tools, supplies, parts, personal protective equipment, and related shop materials. • Supports daily shop readiness by preparing work areas, securing tools and equipment, checking supplies, and ensuring the shop is ready for safe and efficient operations at the start and end of assigned shifts. • Maintains appropriate inventory levels for assigned supplies, parts, tools, personal protective equipment, and shop equipment. • Keeps accurate written records of work performed, parts used, service status, customer concerns, and related vehicle maintenance or repair activity. (15% time)

Customer Service, Coordination, and Workflow Support • Coordinates with the Lead Technician and office staff to support timely repair of customer vehicles and communicate repair status, delays, additional service needs, or other issues affecting vehicle availability. • Responds to after-hours emergencies as assigned and coordinates with the Lead Technician, Fleet Services Manager, office staff, or customers as needed to address urgent vehicle or equipment needs. • Communicates clearly and professionally with customers regarding vehicle concerns, completed repairs, recommended follow-up, expected timelines, and service limitations. • Explains work performed on vehicles to customers when required, using plain language that supports customer understanding and confidence in Fleet Services. • Consults with the Lead Technician to determine when vehicles should be referred to outside contractors for extensive repairs and helps coordinate related next steps. • Identifies recurring vehicle issues, service delays, communication gaps, or repair process concerns and brings them to the attention of the Lead Technician or Fleet Services Manager. • Directs the work of student assistants as necessary. (10% time)

Safety, Chemical Handling, and Compliance • Practices safe work techniques and follows applicable OSHA guidelines, University safety requirements, shop standards, manufacturer guidelines, and department procedures. • Uses required personal protective equipment, including safety glasses, gloves, protective footwear, hearing protection, face shields, respirators, or other assigned protective gear based on the task, equipment, chemical, or work environment. • Ensures personal protective equipment is used properly, maintained in serviceable condition, and replaced or reported when damaged, missing, or no longer effective. • Properly handles, labels, seals, stores, uses, and disposes of chemicals, fluids, lubricants, fuels, solvents, cleaners, batteries, and other hazardous or regulated materials in accordance with applicable safety, environmental, and department procedures. • Responds to chemical spills, leaks, or releases by following established containment, cleanup, mitigation, reporting, and disposal procedures. • Reports unsafe activities, conditions, equipment, personal protective equipment concerns, chemical handling issues, spills, leaks, or work practices to the Lead Technician or Fleet Services Manager. (10% time)

Operational Support for Transportation Services • Provides operational support for Transportation Services. • Participates in the development and implementation of the department’s mission, goals, and strategic planning. • Assists in the review of operations and services to identify efficiencies and integrate best practices. • Coordinates and/or participates in special projects and assignments, the scope of which may extend beyond day-to-day operations. (10% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.

Ability to work with limited oversight.
Working knowledge of automotive fuel systems.

Ability to communicate effectively in English using appropriate automotive vocabulary to obtain and explain procedures relating to automotive repairs, service and maintenance. Interpersonal skills to communicate effectively with other workers to include office staff ensuring clear and direct exchange of information.
Thorough knowledge of department and University policies and procedures.
Ability to efficiently use a computer and related software, to include an automotive work order system (such as Agile FleetCommander), Outlook, and Microsoft Office suite.

Demonstrated skill in the use of standard automotive tools and equipment used on automobiles. Knowledge and ability to safely handle hazardous materials typically found in an automotive repair yard, such as used oils, batteries, and auto shop chemicals.
Ability to read and understand technical automotive manuals.
Ability to read and interpret measurement and diagnostic equipment.
Ability to write clear and concise diagnostic and maintenance reports.
Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations such as adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing.
Ability to lift, carry, stack and move objects weighing 50 to 70 pounds.
Ability to move about the Corporation Yard and campus to gather information, materials and authorizations.

Ability to work under pressure with frequent interruptions and to meet deadlines by efficiently organizing, prioritizing and overlapping work, as well as using non-maintenance time wisely on job related work.
Competency in providing good customer service and resolving problems with a pleasant and diplomatic demeanor.
Ability to withstand exposure and possible skin contact to automotive chemicals, fluids and oils.
